words.gloss: things that are fit to be done
things that are fit to be done

literal: By doing those things which are not fit to be done, one will be ruined; by not doing those things which are fit to be done, one will also be ruined.
translation: One is ruined by doing what ought not to be done; one is also ruined by failing to do what ought to be done.
modern: செய்யத்தகாத செயல்களைச் செய்வதனாலும் ஒருவன் அழிவான்; செய்யத்தக்க செயல்களைச் செய்யாமல் விடுவதனாலும் அவன் அழிவான்.
explanation: This couplet explains that ruin comes from two types of errors: commission and omission. The first line states that performing actions that are improper or unfit (cey-takka alla) leads to destruction. The second line warns that failing to perform actions that are necessary and proper (cey-takka) also leads to the exact same ruin. A wise person must therefore balance action and inaction, knowing both what to avoid and what to execute.
